title: i18next
description: The preset for i18next. It reads namespaces, getFixedT, typed TFunction parameters and plural keys.
---

The `i18next` preset supports [i18next](https://www.i18next.com) without a framework binding. For React, see [react-i18next](/presets/react-i18next).

## Detection

The preset applies when the project depends on `i18next`. The [`react-i18next`](/presets/react-i18next) preset includes this one. If both apply, x18n adds the shared plugins one time.

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  presets: ['i18next'],
})
```

## Namespaces

The preset sets the namespace separator to `:` and the default namespace to `translation`, as i18next does. With a resource pattern that has `{namespace}`, keys have the form `namespace:path`:

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  resources: [
    { pattern: 'public/locales/{locale}/{namespace}.json' }
  ],
})
```

A key without a namespace, such as `t('title')`, is in the `translation` namespace. The preset reads `defaultNS` and `fallbackNS` from the i18next init code (a file such as `src/i18n.ts`). A key that is not in its own namespace is then looked up in the fallback namespaces, in order. Set `namespace.default` and `namespace.fallback` to override them:

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  namespace: {
    default: 'app',
    fallback: ['common']
  },
})
```

To use another separator, such as `t('common|save')` with the i18next option `nsSeparator: '|'`, set `namespace.separator`. Completion writes keys with the same separator.

With `{namespaces}`, a namespace can sit in folders. The preset sets `namespace.fromPath` to `slash`, so `public/locales/en/pages/home.json` is the namespace `pages/home`, as in `t('pages/home:title')`.

## Supported syntax

```ts
import i18next from 'i18next'

i18next.t('common:save')
i18next.t('save', { ns: 'common' })
t('pages.home.title')

const tc = i18next.getFixedT('de', 'common', 'buttons')
tc('save') // common:buttons.save

function label(t: TFunction) {
  return t('app.title')
}

function typeLabel(t: TFunction<'shared'>) {
  return t('type.bug') // shared:type.bug
}

t($ => $.app.title)
```

- `t`, `i18next.t` and `i18n.t` are translate calls. The `ns` option in the second argument sets the namespace.
- `getFixedT(lng, ns, keyPrefix)` returns a `t` with a namespace and a key prefix.
- A parameter or prop with the type `TFunction` is a translate function. Its first type argument is the namespace: `TFunction<'shared'>`, or the first of `TFunction<['shared', 'common']>`. Props work when typed inline (`{ t }: { t: TFunction<'shared'> }`) or with an interface or type of the same file.
- The selector form `t($ => $.a.b)` reads the key `a.b`.
- In Astro components, such as with astro-i18next, the preset reads the calls in the `---` frontmatter, in `<script>` and in `{...}` template expressions.

## Derived keys

The preset adds the derived key rules `{key}_ordinal_{ordinal}`, `{key}_{plural}` and `{key}_*`. When `t('item')` is used, `item_one`, `item_other` and `item_male` count as used, and `t('item')` is not reported missing. Suffixes stack, so context with plural (`item_male_one`) and ordinal plurals (`item_ordinal_one`) also belong to `item`. Hovers and inline values show the `_other` form, or another form when the locale has no `_other`.

Each locale needs the plural categories of its own language, from `Intl.PluralRules`. With `item_one` and `item_other` in English:

- Japanese needs only `item_other`, and `item_one` is not reported missing there.
- Russian needs `item_one`, `item_few`, `item_many` and `item_other`. The `missing-translation` check reports `item_few` and `item_many` at the English `item_other`, and its fix copies that value.
- A form that a language does not have, such as `item_zero` in English, is optional in every locale.

The translate prompt tells the agent the plural categories of the target locale, for example "i18next plural keys end in _one,_other for de; write one key per category."

## Placeholders

- Interpolation: `{{name}}`, `{{name, format}}` and `{{- raw}}`.
- Nesting: `$t(key)`. The nested key counts as used.

## Extraction templates

| Kinds | Template | Imports |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `js-string`, `js-template` | `i18next.t('{key}'{args})` | `import i18next from 'i18next'` |

The preset applies when the project depends on `i18next`. The [`react-i18next`](/presets/react-i18next) preset includes this one. If both apply, x18n adds the shared plugins one time.

```ts [x18n.config.ts]

export default defineConfig({

})
```

## Namespaces

The preset sets the namespace separator to `:` and the default namespace to `translation`, as i18next does. With a resource pattern that has `{namespace}`, keys have the form `namespace:path`:

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  resources: [
    { pattern: 'public/locales/{locale}/{namespace}.json' }
  ],
})
```

A key without a namespace, such as `t('title')`, is in the `translation` namespace. The preset reads `defaultNS` and `fallbackNS` from the i18next init code (a file such as `src/i18n.ts`). A key that is not in its own namespace is then looked up in the fallback namespaces, in order. Set `namespace.default` and `namespace.fallback` to override them:

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

  namespace: {
    default: 'app',
    fallback: ['common']
  },
})
```

To use another separator, such as `t('common|save')` with the i18next option `nsSeparator: '|'`, set `namespace.separator`. Completion writes keys with the same separator.

With `{namespaces}`, a namespace can sit in folders. The preset sets `namespace.fromPath` to `slash`, so `public/locales/en/pages/home.json` is the namespace `pages/home`, as in `t('pages/home:title')`.

## Supported syntax

```ts
import i18next from 'i18next'

i18next.t('common:save')
i18next.t('save', { ns: 'common' })
t('pages.home.title')

const tc = i18next.getFixedT('de', 'common', 'buttons')
tc('save') // common:buttons.save

function label(t: TFunction) {
  return t('app.title')
}

function typeLabel(t: TFunction<'shared'>) {
  return t('type.bug') // shared:type.bug
}

t($ => $.app.title)
```

- In Astro components, such as with astro-i18next, the preset reads the calls in the `---` frontmatter, in `<script>` and in `{...}` template expressions.

## Derived keys

The preset adds the derived key rules `{key}_ordinal_{ordinal}`, `{key}_{plural}` and `{key}_*`. When `t('item')` is used, `item_one`, `item_other` and `item_male` count as used, and `t('item')` is not reported missing. Suffixes stack, so context with plural (`item_male_one`) and ordinal plurals (`item_ordinal_one`) also belong to `item`. - A form that a language does not have, such as `item_zero` in English, is optional in every locale.

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  resources: [
    { pattern: 'public/locales/{locale}/{namespace}.json' }
  ],
})
```

A key without a namespace, such as `t('title')`, is in the `translation` namespace. The preset reads `defaultNS` and `fallbackNS` from the i18next init code (a file such as `src/i18n.ts`). A key that is not in its own namespace is then looked up in the fallback namespaces, in order. Set `namespace.default` and `namespace.fallback` to override them:

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  namespace: {
    default: 'app',
    fallback: ['common']
  },
})
```

To use another separator, such as `t('common|save')` with the i18next option `nsSeparator: '|'`, set `namespace.separator`. Completion writes keys with the same separator.

With `{namespaces}`, a namespace can sit in folders. The preset sets `namespace.fromPath` to `slash`, so `public/locales/en/pages/home.json` is the namespace `pages/home`, as in `t('pages/home:title')`.

## Supported syntax

```ts
import i18next from 'i18next'

i18next.t('common:save')
i18next.t('save', { ns: 'common' })
t('pages.home.title')

const tc = i18next.getFixedT('de', 'common', 'buttons')
tc('save') // common:buttons.save

function label(t: TFunction) {
  return t('app.title')
}

function typeLabel(t: TFunction<'shared'>) {
  return t('type.bug') // shared:type.bug
}

t($ => $.app.title)
```

- `t`, `i18next.t` and `i18n.t` are translate calls. The `ns` option in the second argument sets the namespace.
- `getFixedT(lng, ns, keyPrefix)` returns a `t` with a namespace and a key prefix.
- A parameter or prop with the type `TFunction` is a translate function. Its first type argument is the namespace: `TFunction<'shared'>`, or the first of `TFunction<['shared', 'common']>`. Props work when typed inline (`{ t }: { t: TFunction<'shared'> }`) or with an interface or type of the same file.
- The selector form `t($ => $.a.b)` reads the key `a.b`.
- In Astro components, such as with astro-i18next, the preset reads the calls in the `---` frontmatter, in `<script>` and in `{...}` template expressions.

## Derived keys

The preset adds the derived key rules `{key}_ordinal_{ordinal}`, `{key}_{plural}` and `{key}_*`. When `t('item')` is used, `item_one`, `item_other` and `item_male` count as used, and `t('item')` is not reported missing. Suffixes stack, so context with plural (`item_male_one`) and ordinal plurals (`item_ordinal_one`) also belong to `item`. Hovers and inline values show the `_other` form, or another form when the locale has no `_other`.

Each locale needs the plural categories of its own language, from `Intl.PluralRules`. With `item_one` and `item_other` in English:

- Japanese needs only `item_other`, and `item_one` is not reported missing there.
- Russian needs `item_one`, `item_few`, `item_many` and `item_other`. The `missing-translation` check reports `item_few` and `item_many` at the English `item_other`, and its fix copies that value.
- A form that a language does not have, such as `item_zero` in English, is optional in every locale.

The translate prompt tells the agent the plural categories of the target locale, for example "i18next plural keys end in _one,_other for de; write one key per category."

The `i18next` preset supports [i18next](https://www.i18next.com) without a framework binding. For React, see [react-i18next](/presets/react-i18next).

## Detection

The preset applies when the project depends on `i18next`. The [`react-i18next`](/presets/react-i18next) preset includes this one. If both apply, x18n adds the shared plugins one time.

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  presets: ['i18next'],
})
```

## Namespaces

The preset sets the namespace separator to `:` and the default namespace to `translation`, as i18next does. With a resource pattern that has `{namespace}`, keys have the form `namespace:path`:

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  resources: [
    { pattern: 'public/locales/{locale}/{namespace}.json' }
  ],
})
```

A key without a namespace, such as `t('title')`, is in the `translation` namespace. The preset reads `defaultNS` and `fallbackNS` from the i18next init code (a file such as `src/i18n.ts`). A key that is not in its own namespace is then looked up in the fallback namespaces, in order. Set `namespace.default` and `namespace.fallback` to override them:

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  namespace: {
    default: 'app',
    fallback: ['common']
  },
})
```

To use another separator, such as `t('common|save')` with the i18next option `nsSeparator: '|'`, set `namespace.separator`. Completion writes keys with the same separator.

With `{namespaces}`, a namespace can sit in folders. The preset sets `namespace.fromPath` to `slash`, so `public/locales/en/pages/home.json` is the namespace `pages/home`, as in `t('pages/home:title')`.

## Supported syntax

```ts
import i18next from 'i18next'

i18next.t('common:save')
i18next.t('save', { ns: 'common' })
t('pages.home.title')

const tc = i18next.getFixedT('de', 'common', 'buttons')
tc('save') // common:buttons.save

function label(t: TFunction) {
  return t('app.title')
}

function typeLabel(t: TFunction<'shared'>) {
  return t('type.bug') // shared:type.bug
}

t($ => $.app.title)
```

- `t`, `i18next.t` and `i18n.t` are translate calls. The `ns` option in the second argument sets the namespace.
- `getFixedT(lng, ns, keyPrefix)` returns a `t` with a namespace and a key prefix.
- A parameter or prop with the type `TFunction` is a translate function. Its first type argument is the namespace: `TFunction<'shared'>`, or the first of `TFunction<['shared', 'common']>`. Props work when typed inline (`{ t }: { t: TFunction<'shared'> }`) or with an interface or type of the same file.
- The selector form `t($ => $.a.b)` reads the key `a.b`.
- In Astro components, such as with astro-i18next, the preset reads the calls in the `---` frontmatter, in `<script>` and in `{...}` template expressions.

## Derived keys

The preset adds the derived key rules `{key}_ordinal_{ordinal}`, `{key}_{plural}` and `{key}_*`. When `t('item')` is used, `item_one`, `item_other` and `item_male` count as used, and `t('item')` is not reported missing. Suffixes stack, so context with plural (`item_male_one`) and ordinal plurals (`item_ordinal_one`) also belong to `item`. Hovers and inline values show the `_other` form, or another form when the locale has no `_other`.

Each locale needs the plural categories of its own language, from `Intl.PluralRules`. With `item_one` and `item_other` in English:

- Japanese needs only `item_other`, and `item_one` is not reported missing there.
- Russian needs `item_one`, `item_few`, `item_many` and `item_other`. The `missing-translation` check reports `item_few` and `item_many` at the English `item_other`, and its fix copies that value.
- A form that a language does not have, such as `item_zero` in English, is optional in every locale.

The translate prompt tells the agent the plural categories of the target locale, for example "i18next plural keys end in _one,_other for de; write one key per category."

## Placeholders

- Interpolation: `{{name}}`, `{{name, format}}` and `{{- raw}}`.
- Nesting: `$t(key)`. The nested key counts as used.

## Extraction templates

| Kinds | Template | Imports |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `js-string`, `js-template` | `i18next.t('{key}'{args})` | `import i18next from 'i18next'` |

title: gravity-ui-i18n
description: The preset for @gravity-ui/i18n. It reads i18n.i18n(keyset, key) calls, keyset functions and keyset folders.
---

The `gravity-ui-i18n` preset supports [@gravity-ui/i18n](https://github.com/gravity-ui/i18n).

## Detection

The preset applies when the project depends on `@gravity-ui/i18n`.

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  presets: ['gravity-ui-i18n'],
})
```

## Locale files

If your config has no `resources`, the preset uses these patterns:

- `src/i18n-keysets/{namespaces}/{locale}.json`: one folder per keyset. The folder `page.home` holds the keyset `page.home`.
- `src/**/{namespace}/i18n/{locale}.json`: an `i18n` folder next to a component. The component folder names the keyset, so `src/components/Header/i18n/en.json` holds the keyset `Header`.

If neither pattern matches a file, x18n guesses the locale directories. A file such as `src/i18n/en.json` can then hold every keyset as a top-level object.

## Keysets

A keyset is the first part of the key. `i18n.i18n('page.home', 'title')` is a usage of `page.home.title`, both in `src/i18n-keysets/page.home/en.json` and in one `en.json` with `{ "page.home": { "title": "..." } }`.

A plural key is an object with the CLDR forms `zero`, `one`, `two`, `few`, `many` and `other`. A usage of the key counts as a usage of each form.

## Supported syntax

```ts [src/App.tsx]
import { I18N } from '@gravity-ui/i18n'

const i18n = new I18N()

i18n.i18n('common', 'hello') // common.hello

const keyset = i18n.keyset('wizard')
keyset('label_no-access') // wizard.label_no-access

const i18nHome = i18n.bind(null, 'page.home')
i18nHome('title', { name }) // page.home.title
```

- `i18n.i18n(keyset, key)` and `i18nInstance.i18n(keyset, key)` are translate calls.
- `i18n.keyset(keyset)` and `i18nInstance.keyset(keyset)` return a translate function for the keyset.
- `i18n.bind(null, keyset)` and `i18nInstance.i18n.bind(i18nInstance, keyset)` do the same.

A bare `i18n(keyset, key)` is not read, because projects also name a keyset function `i18n`, and then `i18n('key', 'x')` takes no keyset. A keyset that is no string literal, such as `i18n.i18n(getKeyset(), 'title')`, makes the usage dynamic.

For an instance with another name, add its callees to `usage.calls`. A keyset function that a module exports, such as `export default i18n.keyset('Button')`, is not followed into the modules that import it.

## Placeholders

Double braces: `{{name}}`.

## Extraction templates

The preset adds none, as an extracted key needs its keyset as a separate argument. Set `extract.templates` for your keyset functions.

A plural key is an object with the CLDR forms `zero`, `one`, `two`, `few`, `many` and `other`. A usage of the key counts as a usage of each form.

keyset('label_no-access') // wizard.label_no-access

i18nHome('title', { name }) // page.home.title

title: 'X18N1003: Unknown preset'
description: 'Unknown preset. Use a preset name listed in the docs, or a preset object.'
---

<!-- Generated by docs/scripts/generate.ts from the source code. Do not edit. -->

## Message

```
[X18N1003] Unknown preset <detail>
├▶ fix: Use a preset name listed in the docs, or a preset object.
╰▶ see: https://x18n.dev/errors/x18n1003
```

The CLI prints the code and why the error happened, with details such as a file name or a field. The fix and a link to this page follow. With `--json`, the same parts are in `errors` of the [envelope](/references/json-contracts).

## What to do

A string in `presets` is not the name of a built-in preset, and x18n has no plugin loader in this runtime.

1. Use a name from the [presets list](/presets).
2. Or pass a preset object from a TS config, for example `presets: [vueI18n()]`.

## Exit code

The CLI exits with code `2`.

---
title: 'Glossary'
description: 'The names that x18n uses in its code, docs and UI.'
---

<!-- Generated by docs/scripts/generate.ts from the source code. Do not edit. -->

x18n uses one name for each idea, in code, docs and UI. The "Not" column lists names that x18n avoids for the same idea. [Concepts](/guide/concepts) explains the most important ones with examples.

| Term | Meaning | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Project** | One i18n setup with one root, one config and one set of locales. A monorepo can have many. | workspace (that is the editor's word), app |
| **Host** | The object that gives a project file access, globbing, watching and caching. | adapter, driver, fs |
| **Locale** | A locale code exactly as written in paths and files (`en`, `zh_CN`). Never normalized. | language, lang (except in i18n-ally migration text) |
| **Source locale** | The locale that is the source of truth for checks and prompts. | base, default language |
| **Display locale** | The locale shown in annotations and hovers. Per user. | |
| **Resource** | A file, or a block inside a file, that holds messages for one locale and one namespace. | locale file (fine in prose for users), dictionary |
| **Namespace** | A named group of keys, usually from a file name. | scope (that is a code region) |
| **Key** | The canonical id of a message: namespace plus path. String form `ns:a.b.c`. | keypath, id |
| **Message** | The value of one key in one locale. | translation (fine for non-source locales in prose), string |
| **Usage** | One occurrence of a key in source code. | reference, occurrence |
| **Prefix usage** | A dynamic usage with a static prefix (`t(`pages.${id}.title`)`). It makes every key under the prefix "possibly" used. | partial key |
| **Callee set** | The names that count as translate calls in a file: declared names, same-file aliases, wrappers, typed params. | |
| **Subtree rename** | Renaming a parent node, which renames every key under it. | prefix rename (fine in UI labels) |
| **Scope** | A region of source code with a default namespace or key prefix. | |
| **Hard string** | Text in source code that should probably be a message. | |
| **Plugin** | An object that contributes capabilities through the plugin API. | framework, extension |
| **Preset** | A detected or listed group of plugins for one library. | framework |
| **Capability** | One kind of contribution: manifest reader, locale finder, format, scanner, extractor, check, reporter, placeholder syntax, history provider, review store. | |
| **Format** | Reads and writes one file format. | parser (only for the read half) |
| **Locale finder** | Finds resources. | loader |
| **Scanner** | Finds usages in source files. | detector |
| **Extractor** | Finds hard strings and builds replacements. | |
| **Check** | Produces diagnostics from project state. `x18n check` runs all checks. | rule (fine inside extraction scoring), lint |
| **History provider** | Reports when each message last changed, for stale translations. Git is the built-in one. | blame, freshness source |
| **Stale translation** | A target message that last changed before its source message did. | outdated key (fine in UI labels) |
| **Reporter** | Turns diagnostics and analysis into text output. | formatter |
| **Diagnostic** | One reported issue with a code, severity and optional fixes. | problem, error (unless severity is error) |
| **Plan** | The side-effect-free result of planning edits: file changes plus decisions. | patch, diff |
| **Decision** | A question in a plan that a surface must answer before apply. | prompt (that word is for LLM prompts) |
| **In-place annotation** | Editor decoration that hides a key and shows its display-locale value. | inline translation |
| **Surface** | A user-facing layer on the core: CLI, LSP, extension, UI, MCP. | client, frontend |
| **Translate prompt** | The text that describes translation work for an agent or LLM. | |
| **Review** | One comment on one message: a `comment`, an `approve`, a `request-change` or a `suggestion`. | review comment (fine in UI labels), note |
| **Review thread** | The reviews of one message, oldest first, with a state from its open reviews. | conversation |
| **Review store** | Reads and writes the review file (`.x18n/reviews.yml`). The YAML one is built in. | |

title: 'dynamic-key'
description: 'A fully dynamic key that no check can follow.'
---

<!-- Generated by docs/scripts/generate.ts from the source code. Do not edit. -->

A fully dynamic key that no check can follow.

The check is off by default.

A fully dynamic key, such as `t(key)`, has no static prefix. No check can follow it. Turn this check on to find such usages.

## Configure

Turn the check on in `checks`:

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  checks: {
    'dynamic-key': 'warning',
  },
})
```

`x18n check --only dynamic-key` runs this check alone. `x18n check --skip dynamic-key` skips it for one run.

description: 'A fully dynamic key that no check can follow.'

<!-- Generated by docs/scripts/generate.ts from the source code. Do not edit. -->

A fully dynamic key that no check can follow.

The check is off by default.

A fully dynamic key, such as `t(key)`, has no static prefix. No check can follow it. Turn this check on to find such usages.

## Configure

Turn the check on in `checks`:

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  checks: {
    'dynamic-key': 'warning',
  },
})
```

`x18n check --only dynamic-key` runs this check alone. `x18n check --skip dynamic-key` skips it for one run.

args:
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'

jobs:
  release:
    uses: sxzz/workflows/.github/workflows/release.yml@main
    with:
      publish: true
      # Build before publishing so `packages/cli/skills` (copied by the tsdown hook) exists when files are packed.
      build: pnpm build
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write

  # Publishes the VS Code extension to the Marketplace, Open VSX and the GitHub
  # release. Runs after `release`, which creates the release page vsxpub uploads to.
  extension:
    needs: release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: lts/*
          cache: pnpm

      - run: pnpm install

      - name: Package extension
        working-directory: packages/vscode
        run: |
          pnpm run ext:package
          version=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
          mv x18n.vsix "x18n-$version.vsix"

      - name: Publish extension
        working-directory: packages/vscode
        run: pnpm exec vsxpub --name x18n --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --tag "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --no-dependencies
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VSCE_PAT: ${{ secrets.VSCE_PAT }}
          OVSX_PAT: ${{ secrets.OVSX_PAT }}

title: 'review-changes-requested'
description: 'A message with an open "request change" review.'
---

<!-- Generated by docs/scripts/generate.ts from the source code. Do not edit. -->

A message with an open "request change" review.

The check is on by default, with the severity `info`.

The check reports each message whose open review comments end in a change request, at the message in the reviewed locale. The quick fix resolves the request. A later approval by anyone clears it too. See [Reviews](/guide/reviews).

## Configure

Change the severity, or turn the check off, in `checks`:

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  checks: {
    'review-changes-requested': 'off',
  },
})
```

`x18n check --only review-changes-requested` runs this check alone. `x18n check --skip review-changes-requested` skips it for one run.

## Source

- [`packages/builtins/src/checks/index.ts`](https://github.com/x18n-dev/x18n/blob/main/packages/builtins/src/checks/index.ts)

title: vscode-extension
description: The preset for VS Code extensions. It reads vscode.l10n.t, package.nls.json files and l10n bundles.
---

The `vscode-extension` preset supports the localization of [VS Code extensions](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api#l10n): `vscode.l10n.t` in code, and `%key%` references in `package.json`.

## Detection

The preset applies when the project depends on `vscode` or `@types/vscode`.

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  presets: ['vscode-extension'],
})
```

## Locale files

The preset adds a locale finder for the two file layouts of VS Code:

| File | Locale |
| --- | --- |
| `package.nls.json` | The source locale |
| `package.nls.<locale>.json`, for example `package.nls.de.json` | `<locale>` |
| `l10n/bundle.l10n.json` | The source locale |
| `l10n/bundle.l10n.<locale>.json` | `<locale>` |

The finder looks for these names in any directory, except `node_modules`.

## Supported syntax

`l10n.t` and `vscode.l10n.t` are translate calls:

```ts
import { l10n } from 'vscode'

l10n.t('Hello {0}', name)
```

The preset also adds a regex scanner for JSON files. It reads `"%key%"` references, so the strings of `package.json` count as usages:

```json [package.json]
{
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "command": "ext.hello", "title": "%command.hello%" }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Placeholders

Braces: `{0}`, `{name}`.

description: The preset for VS Code extensions. It reads vscode.l10n.t, package.nls.json files and l10n bundles.
---

The `vscode-extension` preset supports the localization of [VS Code extensions](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/vscode-api#l10n): `vscode.l10n.t` in code, and `%key%` references in `package.json`.

## Detection

The preset applies when the project depends on `vscode` or `@types/vscode`.

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  presets: ['vscode-extension'],
})
```

## Locale files

The preset adds a locale finder for the two file layouts of VS Code:

| File | Locale |
| --- | --- |
| `package.nls.json` | The source locale |
| `package.nls.<locale>.json`, for example `package.nls.de.json` | `<locale>` |
| `l10n/bundle.l10n.json` | The source locale |
| `l10n/bundle.l10n.<locale>.json` | `<locale>` |

The finder looks for these names in any directory, except `node_modules`.

## Supported syntax

`l10n.t` and `vscode.l10n.t` are translate calls:

```ts
import { l10n } from 'vscode'

l10n.t('Hello {0}', name)
```

The preset also adds a regex scanner for JSON files. It reads `"%key%"` references, so the strings of `package.json` count as usages:

```json [package.json]
{
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "command": "ext.hello", "title": "%command.hello%" }
    ]
  }
}
```

x18n found a config file, but it failed to run or read it. The message holds the error from the loader.

1. Fix the syntax error that the message names.
2. Make sure that a TS or JS config has a default export, for example `export default defineConfig({ ... })`.
3. Run `x18n doctor` to see which config file x18n picked.

The CLI exits with code `2`.

title: cargo-i18n
description: The preset for cargo-i18n with Fluent in Rust. It reads i18n.toml, the .ftl files and the fl! macro of i18n-embed-fl.
---

The `cargo-i18n` preset supports [cargo-i18n](https://github.com/kellpossible/cargo-i18n) with the Fluent system: the `i18n-embed` and `i18n-embed-fl` crates.

## Detection

The preset applies when `Cargo.toml` has the dependency `i18n-embed-fl` or `i18n-embed`. x18n reads `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]`, `[build-dependencies]`, `[workspace.dependencies]` and the target dependency tables. For a renamed dependency, such as `fl = { package = "i18n-embed-fl", version = "0.10" }`, x18n sees the alias `fl` and does not detect the preset, so list it.

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  presets: ['cargo-i18n'],
})
```

## Locale files

The preset reads `i18n.toml` in the project root:

```toml [i18n.toml]
fallback_language = "en-US"

[fluent]
assets_dir = "i18n"
```

`fallback_language` is the source locale. If your config has no `resources`, the preset uses `{assets_dir}/{locale}/*.ftl`, so `i18n/en-US/my_crate.ftl`. Without `assets_dir`, the folder is `i18n`.

## Supported syntax

In Rust files, the preset reads the `fl!` macro. The first argument can be the loader, or it can be absent when you use a wrapper macro:

```rust [src/main.rs]
fl!(LANGUAGE_LOADER, "hello-arg", name = "Bob");
fl!(loader, "login", "title");
fl!("hello-world");
```

These usages are `hello-arg`, `login` and `hello-world`. A used message also uses its attributes, so `login.title` is not unused.

## Placeholders

Fluent: `{ $name }`.

## Extraction templates

| Kinds | Template |
| --- | --- |
| any | `fl!(LANGUAGE_LOADER, "{key}")` |

## Limitations

- The gettext system of cargo-i18n (the `tr!` macro and `.po` files) is not supported.
- x18n reads only the `i18n.toml` in the project root. In a workspace with one `i18n.toml` per crate, set `resources` yourself.

The `cargo-i18n` preset supports [cargo-i18n](https://github.com/kellpossible/cargo-i18n) with the Fluent system: the `i18n-embed` and `i18n-embed-fl` crates.

## Detection

The preset applies when `Cargo.toml` has the dependency `i18n-embed-fl` or `i18n-embed`. x18n reads `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]`, `[build-dependencies]`, `[workspace.dependencies]` and the target dependency tables. For a renamed dependency, such as `fl = { package = "i18n-embed-fl", version = "0.10" }`, x18n sees the alias `fl` and does not detect the preset, so list it.

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  presets: ['cargo-i18n'],
})
```

## Locale files

The preset reads `i18n.toml` in the project root:

```toml [i18n.toml]
fallback_language = "en-US"

[fluent]
assets_dir = "i18n"
```

`fallback_language` is the source locale. If your config has no `resources`, the preset uses `{assets_dir}/{locale}/*.ftl`, so `i18n/en-US/my_crate.ftl`. Without `assets_dir`, the folder is `i18n`.

## Supported syntax

In Rust files, the preset reads the `fl!` macro. The first argument can be the loader, or it can be absent when you use a wrapper macro:

```rust [src/main.rs]
fl!(LANGUAGE_LOADER, "hello-arg", name = "Bob");
fl!(loader, "login", "title");
fl!("hello-world");
```

These usages are `hello-arg`, `login` and `hello-world`. A used message also uses its attributes, so `login.title` is not unused.

## Placeholders

Fluent: `{ $name }`.

## Extraction templates

| Kinds | Template |
| --- | --- |
| any | `fl!(LANGUAGE_LOADER, "{key}")` |

## Limitations

- The gettext system of cargo-i18n (the `tr!` macro and `.po` files) is not supported.
- x18n reads only the `i18n.toml` in the project root. In a workspace with one `i18n.toml` per crate, set `resources` yourself.

The preset applies when `Cargo.toml` has the dependency `i18n-embed-fl` or `i18n-embed`. x18n reads `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]`, `[build-dependencies]`, `[workspace.dependencies]` and the target dependency tables. })

fallback_language = "en-US"

[fluent]
assets_dir = "i18n"

description: The preset for cargo-i18n with Fluent in Rust. It reads i18n.toml, the .ftl files and the fl! macro of i18n-embed-fl.
---

The `cargo-i18n` preset supports [cargo-i18n](https://github.com/kellpossible/cargo-i18n) with the Fluent system: the `i18n-embed` and `i18n-embed-fl` crates.

## Detection

The preset applies when `Cargo.toml` has the dependency `i18n-embed-fl` or `i18n-embed`. x18n reads `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]`, `[build-dependencies]`, `[workspace.dependencies]` and the target dependency tables. For a renamed dependency, such as `fl = { package = "i18n-embed-fl", version = "0.10" }`, x18n sees the alias `fl` and does not detect the preset, so list it.

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  presets: ['cargo-i18n'],
})
```

## Locale files

The preset reads `i18n.toml` in the project root:

```toml [i18n.toml]
fallback_language = "en-US"

[fluent]
assets_dir = "i18n"
```

`fallback_language` is the source locale. If your config has no `resources`, the preset uses `{assets_dir}/{locale}/*.ftl`, so `i18n/en-US/my_crate.ftl`. Without `assets_dir`, the folder is `i18n`.

## Supported syntax

In Rust files, the preset reads the `fl!` macro. The first argument can be the loader, or it can be absent when you use a wrapper macro:

```rust [src/main.rs]
fl!(LANGUAGE_LOADER, "hello-arg", name = "Bob");
fl!(loader, "login", "title");
fl!("hello-world");
```

These usages are `hello-arg`, `login` and `hello-world`. A used message also uses its attributes, so `login.title` is not unused.

## Placeholders

Fluent: `{ $name }`.

## Extraction templates

| Kinds | Template |
| --- | --- |
| any | `fl!(LANGUAGE_LOADER, "{key}")` |

## Limitations

- The gettext system of cargo-i18n (the `tr!` macro and `.po` files) is not supported.
- x18n reads only the `i18n.toml` in the project root. In a workspace with one `i18n.toml` per crate, set `resources` yourself.

title: 'Errors'
description: 'Every X18N error code with its title, fix and exit code.'
---

<!-- Generated by docs/scripts/generate.ts from the source code. Do not edit. -->

Each error of x18n has a code such as `X18N0001`. The CLI prints the code with why the error happened, a fix and a link to the page of the code. With `--json`, the error is in `errors` of the [envelope](/references/json-contracts), with a `docs` link to its page here.

The first digit is the group:

- `0`: config.
- `1`: plugins.
- `2`: finding and parsing locale files.
- `3`: scanning source files.
- `4`: edits.

| Code | Title | Exit code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [X18N0001](/errors/x18n0001) | Invalid config | `2` |
| [X18N0002](/errors/x18n0002) | Config file could not be loaded | `2` |
| [X18N0003](/errors/x18n0003) | Unknown project | `2` |
| [X18N1001](/errors/x18n1001) | Plugin could not be loaded | `2` |
| [X18N1002](/errors/x18n1002) | Duplicate capability id | `2` |
| [X18N1003](/errors/x18n1003) | Unknown preset | `2` |
| [X18N1004](/errors/x18n1004) | Invalid YAML plugin | `2` |
| [X18N2001](/errors/x18n2001) | No format for resource | `1` |
| [X18N2002](/errors/x18n2002) | Resource could not be parsed | `1` |
| [X18N2003](/errors/x18n2003) | Resource is not an object of messages | `1` |
| [X18N2004](/errors/x18n2004) | Locale file is not static | `1` |
| [X18N3001](/errors/x18n3001) | Source file could not be scanned | `1` |
| [X18N4001](/errors/x18n4001) | Resource is read-only | `1` |
| [X18N4002](/errors/x18n4002) | Rename target already exists | `1` |
| [X18N4003](/errors/x18n4003) | A decision is needed | `3` |
| [X18N4004](/errors/x18n4004) | Plan is stale | `4` |
| [X18N4005](/errors/x18n4005) | No resource for the key | `1` |
| [X18N4006](/errors/x18n4006) | Key not found | `1` |
| [X18N4007](/errors/x18n4007) | Placeholder mismatch | `1` |
| [X18N4008](/errors/x18n4008) | Invalid edit input | `1` |

# x18n maintainer guide

x18n views and maintains the i18n files of any project, for humans and agents: an editor-neutral core, a CLI, a language server, a VS Code extension, and a devframe UI. The plan lives in [`plans/`](./plans/README.md). Where code and plan disagree, the code and its tests win, and the plan gets fixed.

## Rules that apply everywhere

- **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD** and **MAY** use RFC 2119 meanings. They mark
  real invariants - layer boundaries, wire contracts, output shapes - not house style.
- Before a PR, all gates MUST pass:
  `pnpm lint && pnpm knip && pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build`.
  Commits follow Conventional Commits.
- Names MUST follow [`plans/glossary.md`](./plans/glossary.md) (resource, message, usage, plugin, preset, ...).
- Dependencies go through the pnpm catalogs (`catalog:<name>`); versions MUST NOT be pinned in a `package.json`.

## Boundary invariants

Full list and reasons: [`plans/01-architecture.md`](./plans/01-architecture.md).

- `@x18n/core` MUST NOT import `node:*`, `vscode`, LSP or devframe packages, and MUST NOT name any i18n library or file format.
- `@x18n/builtins` MUST use only the public API of `@x18n/core` and MUST NOT import `node:*`.
- Core MUST NOT prompt or ask; it returns decisions as data and surfaces ask.

- **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD** and **MAY** use RFC 2119 meanings. They mark
  real invariants - layer boundaries, wire contracts, output shapes - not house style.
- Before a PR, all gates MUST pass:

  Commits follow Conventional Commits.
- Names MUST follow [`plans/glossary.md`](./plans/glossary.md) (resource, message, usage, plugin, preset, ...).
- Dependencies go through the pnpm catalogs (`catalog:<name>`); versions MUST NOT be pinned in a `package.json`.

Full list and reasons: [`plans/01-architecture.md`](./plans/01-architecture.md).

# x18n maintainer guide

## Rules that apply everywhere

- **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD** and **MAY** use RFC 2119 meanings. They mark
  real invariants - layer boundaries, wire contracts, output shapes - not house style.
- Before a PR, all gates MUST pass:
  `pnpm lint && pnpm knip && pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build`.
  Commits follow Conventional Commits.
- Names MUST follow [`plans/glossary.md`](./plans/glossary.md) (resource, message, usage, plugin, preset, ...).
- Dependencies go through the pnpm catalogs (`catalog:<name>`); versions MUST NOT be pinned in a `package.json`.

## Boundary invariants

Full list and reasons: [`plans/01-architecture.md`](./plans/01-architecture.md).

- `@x18n/core` MUST NOT import `node:*`, `vscode`, LSP or devframe packages, and MUST NOT name any i18n library or file format.
- `@x18n/builtins` MUST use only the public API of `@x18n/core` and MUST NOT import `node:*`.
- Core MUST NOT prompt or ask; it returns decisions as data and surfaces ask.
- Surfaces (CLI, LSP, UI, extension) reach project state only through the core `Project` API.
- CLI `--json` output, LSP `x18n/*` requests, RPC functions and MCP tools are wire contracts: versioned and covered by schema or snapshot tests.

## Built-ins load on demand

`@x18n/builtins` keeps what decides from what does the work, so a run loads only the modules it needs.

- Presets: each preset is a folder, `src/presets/<name>/`. `entry.ts` is cheap and always loaded: it default-exports
  `{ detect, exclusive?, load: () => import('./index') }`. `index.ts` is the preset, with its helpers beside it, and core
  calls `load` only when `detect` passes or the config lists the preset. A preset module MUST NOT carry `detect` or
  `exclusive`; `entry.ts` MUST NOT statically import the implementation. `src/presets/index.ts` only maps names to
  entries. Code shared by several presets goes in `src/presets/shared/`.
- Formats and scanners follow the same pattern: a folder per format or scanner, `src/formats/<name>/` and
  `src/scanners/<name>/`, with `entry.ts` (`{ extensions, load: () => import('./index') }`, always loaded) and `index.ts`
  (the implementation). Core loads a format when it first reads a file of that extension (`registry.loadFormatFor`) and a
  scanner when it first scans a matching file (`registry.loadScannersFor`); `formatFor` returns only loaded formats.
  `entry.ts` and the module MUST agree on id and extensions (`test/entries.test.ts` checks it).
- `regex` is the exception among scanners: its extensions come from `usage.regex`, so `createBuiltins()` always loads it.
  Reporters are a map of loaders, also loaded by `createBuiltins()`.
- Each module is its own tsdown entry (`@x18n/builtins/<kind>/<name>`, from `<name>/index.ts`) and exports its factory by name and as `default`.
  The `index.ts` of a kind holds only the map. Code shared between modules goes in a `shared/` folder, which is never an entry.
- `src/index.ts` imports the maps through the package name (`@x18n/builtins/presets`) and `tsdown.config.ts` keeps
  them external. Without that, the map and the entry share a chunk with mangled export names, and the tsnapi snapshot
  turns unreadable and changes every build.

## Layout

| Path | Package |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/core` | `@x18n/core` |
| `packages/builtins` | `@x18n/builtins` |
| `packages/node` | `@x18n/node` |
| `packages/cli` | `@x18n/cli` |
| `packages/lsp` | `@x18n/lsp` |
| `packages/ui` | `@x18n/ui` (Nuxt SPA in `app/`, devframe node side in `src/node/`) |
| `packages/devtools` | `@x18n/devtools` (the UI in Vite DevTools, Nuxt DevTools and devframe hubs) |
| `packages/vscode` | `x18n-vscode` (private, published to the Marketplace) |
| `docs` | docs site on the comark-docs layer (`x18n.dev`) |

The root `x18n.config.ts` points x18n at the UI's own messages (`packages/ui/app/locales`), so the repo checks itself.

## Commands

- `pnpm codegen` writes files that typecheck needs (`.nuxt` types, `packages/vscode/src/generated/meta.ts`). It runs on install.
- `pnpm test` builds first; `test/exports.test.ts` snapshots the public API of every published package with tsnapi. Update snapshots with `pnpm test -u` only for intended API changes.
- `pnpm docs` starts the docs site.

title: 'Checks'
description: 'Every built-in check of x18n check, with its default severity.'
---

<!-- Generated by docs/scripts/generate.ts from the source code. Do not edit. -->

A check reads the project and reports diagnostics. A diagnostic is one reported issue with a code, a severity and optional fixes. `x18n check` runs every check, and the editor shows the same diagnostics.

The `recommended` set is every check that is not `off` below. Override the severity of a check in `checks`:

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  checks: {
    'unused-key': 'error',
    'identical-to-source': 'warning',
    'key-style': [
      'warning',
      { case: 'camel' }
    ],
  },
})
```

A severity is `error`, `warning`, `info`, `hint` or `off`. `strict: true` (or `x18n check --strict`) turns every warning into an error. `ignoreKeys` removes keys from every check.

| Check | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [missing-key](/checks/missing-key) | `error` | A usage whose key is not defined in the source locale. |
| [invalid-syntax](/checks/invalid-syntax) | `error` | Message syntax errors (ICU, linked messages, nesting). |
| [placeholder-mismatch](/checks/placeholder-mismatch) | `error` | Target value placeholders differ from the source value. |
| [key-conflict](/checks/key-conflict) | `error` | A key that is both a leaf and a parent, or is duplicated across files of one locale. |
| [missing-translation](/checks/missing-translation) | `warning` | A source-locale key that target locales lack, or a plural form their language needs. One diagnostic per key, at the source entry. |
| [stale-translation](/checks/stale-translation) | `warning` | A translation that last changed before its source message, by the history providers (git). |
| [review-changes-requested](/checks/review-changes-requested) | `info` | A message with an open "request change" review. |
| [empty-translation](/checks/empty-translation) | `warning` | A message with an empty string value. |
| [redundant-translation](/checks/redundant-translation) | `warning` | A message in a locale with a fallback that equals the message it falls back to, so it can be removed. |
| [unused-key](/checks/unused-key) | `warning` | A key with no usage, after keysInUse, derived keys and dynamic prefixes. |
| [locale-code-conflict](/checks/locale-code-conflict) | `warning` | Locale codes that differ only in spelling, such as zh_CN and zh-CN. |
| [dynamic-key](/checks/dynamic-key) | `off` | A fully dynamic key that no check can follow. |
| [identical-to-source](/checks/identical-to-source) | `off` | A target value that equals the source value. |
| [key-style](/checks/key-style) | `off` | A key that does not match a naming rule (options: case, pattern). |
| [hard-string](/checks/hard-string) | `info` | A hard-coded string that should probably be a message. On with `extract.autoDetect`. |
| [glossary](/checks/glossary) | `off` | A glossary term translated differently from the glossary. |
| [invalid-resource](/checks/invalid-resource) | `error` | A locale file or source file that x18n failed to read, parse or scan. |

The reporters of `x18n check --reporter` are `pretty`, `json`, `markdown`, `github`, `sarif`. See [CLI and x18n check](/surfaces/cli#x18n-check-reporters).

--- title: ember-intl description: The preset for ember-intl. It reads the t helper in Handlebars and template-tag files, and intl.t in code. --- The `ember-intl` preset supports [ember-intl](https://ember-intl.github.io/ember-intl). ## Detection The preset applies when the project depends on `ember-intl`. ```ts [x18n.config.ts] import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core' export default defineConfig({ presets: ['ember-intl'], }) ``` ## Locale files If your config has no `resources`, the preset uses `translations/{locale}.{ext}` and `translations/{namespaces}/{locale}.{ext}`. ## Supported syntax In `.hbs`, `.gjs` and `.gts` files, the preset reads the `t` helper, as a mustache and as a subexpression: ```hbs [app/templates/a.hbs]

{{t 'a.b'}}

{{concat (t 'a.c') '!'}}

``` In JS and TS files, `intl.t` is a translate call, also as `this.intl.t`. ## Placeholders ICU MessageFormat, as for [next-intl](/presets/next-intl#placeholders). ## Extraction templates | Kinds | Files | Template | | --- | --- | --- | | any | `**/*.hbs` | `{{t '{key}'}}` | | `js-string`, `js-template` | any | `this.intl.t('{key}'{args})` |

title: php-joomla
description: The preset for Joomla. It reads INI language files and Text::_ calls.
---

The `php-joomla` preset supports the [language files of Joomla](https://docs.joomla.org/Specification_of_language_files).

## Detection

The preset applies when `composer.json` requires `joomla/application` or `joomla/cms`.

```ts [x18n.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@x18n/core'

export default defineConfig({
  presets: ['php-joomla'],
})
```

## Locale files

If your config has no `resources`, the preset uses `language/{locale}/*.ini` and `administrator/language/{locale}/*.ini`. The `ini` format reads and writes these files. Keys stay flat.

```ini [language/en-GB/en-GB.com_demo.ini]
COM_DEMO_TITLE="Demo"

```ini [language/en-GB/en-GB.com_demo.ini]
COM_DEMO_TITLE="Demo"
```

## Supported syntax

In PHP files, the preset reads `Text::_` and the other static methods of `Text`, and the legacy `JText`:

```php [site/view.php]
<?php echo Text::_('COM_DEMO_TITLE'); ?>
```

## Placeholders

printf: `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`.

## Extraction templates

| Kinds | Template |
| --- | --- |
| any | `Text::_('{key}')` |
